title: Universal Music and Sony Want to Know How Many AI-Generated Songs DistroKid Releases
key_facts: Universal Music Group and Sony Music are seeking to require the indie music distributor DistroKid to disclose how many AI-generated songs it uploads each month.
They say they need the data for their ongoing litigation against the AI music platform Suno.

In a new federal court filing this week they said they had subpoenaed DistroKid for its monthly recording submissions and its AI detection tools, and that DistroKid has refused to share any documents.
The filing calls the data 'highly relevant' because the market effect of AI-generated music is a central contested question in the Suno case.
About a month ago, in September, UMG sued DistroKid separately, claiming it helped bad actors upload AI 'slop' songs at mass scale and diluted the royalty pool; Sony is not part of that lawsuit.

The filing says that between March and September 2026 DistroKid distributed nearly 12 million tracks to a single major digital service, more than half of all tracks delivered to that service and more than all other distributors combined.
DistroKid did not immediately respond; it has said it strongly disagrees with UMG's allegations and takes copyright protection and fraud prevention seriously.
quote_evidence: highly relevant information that only DistroKid possesses and are proportional to a case in which the market effect of AI-generated music is a central contested question.

DistroKid distributed nearly 12 million tracks to a single major digital service, comprising more than half of all tracks delivered to that service and exceeding deliveries from all other distributors combined.
We strongly disagree with UMG's allegations and are disappointed that it chose litigation rather than established industry processes to address these issues,
why_it_matters_hint: The labels are using the Suno case to get hard numbers on how much AI music reaches streaming services through one major distributor.
notes: Figures about DistroKid's volume are the labels' claims in a court filing, not independently checked. The Hollywood Reporter text has a minor typo (filed/filing); no other doubt.
